issues.reason: A bare generic's contingent property takes the empirical dial ('Trellises are wooden' / 'Apples are sweet' -> (STV 0.9 0.9); colour is the instruction set's own empirical exemplar in 'all swans are white', and 'when unsure -> empirical'), so (Inheritance mist_light pale) at 1.0/0.99 over-asserts a definitional, exceptionless claim the text does not make.

Same dial: (Inheritance mist_light silver) is a kind-level appearance claim, empirical by the 'could a counterexample exist' test and the unsure-default, so it takes (STV 0.9 0.9), not the taxonomic 1.0/0.99 reserved for the flame kind atom.

new_gaps: Adjective-stacked colour ('a pale silver flame'): the instruction set does not say whether 'pale' modifies the colour term (one shade property) or the head independently (two properties); the parse's two-atom split is an improvisation.
defect_summary: Issue 0: (Inheritance mist_light pale) at (STV 0.9 0.9). Issue 1: (Inheritance mist_light silver) at (STV 0.9 0.9); the genus (Inheritance mist_light light) and kind atom (Inheritance mist_light flame) keep 1.0/0.99.
notes: Compound handling (noun modifier 'mist' unexposed, genus 'light', colour adjectives unfused) is correct; the only fault is the truth-value dial on the two appearance atoms.
